speaker: SPEAKER_03
transcript: Well, I think what I'm doing is reaching back to the historical roots of the Republican Party with people like Teddy Roosevelt, and they were conservationists that wanted to leave what we were given from God better than we found it. But part of the reason we wanted to do that is because we want to enjoy the beautiful, natural environment. We want to be able to pass that on to our kids and grandkids to be able to enjoy. I think what the left is doing, they get off on the global warming stuff, And they basically want to use that as a pretext to do policies they would want to impose on society anyways. So I'm not doing any of that. What I'm doing is focusing on things that actually impact people's lives. And when I became governor, I had kind of the sugar industry opposed me a lot of policy in Florida. had been more geared toward kind of helping that industry to the exclusion of some of the other things. So there was a lot of communities that have been very frustrated with that. So I said, look, I'm going to move forward. I'm going to get it done. We're going to be in a good spot. So I came into office. We did a big executive order, reoriented policy. We also eventually passed a bill for water quality with the legislature. But I said, I am going to put real money on to get the infrastructure in place that you need to. So for example, Lake Okeechobee, When that would rise, it's controlled by the Army Corps of Engineers, they would spew the water out into the estuary that would go out to the west coast and east coast of Florida. The problem is, there's a lot of runoff that goes into Lake Okeechobee. There's a lot of nutrients, so it ends up sparking things like algae blooms. Well, that's not good. So what we've done is we've accelerated a lot of the water infrastructure. We now have a reservoir that's complete on the east side of Lake Okeechobee. We're going to have one complete on the west side, and then we've done a lot to accelerate this reservoir south of Lake Okeechobee. We've also made infrastructure improvements to say, like, raise some of the bridges so that more water can go on raising roads. So you now have the way God intended the Florida Everglades was that water would flow down through the Everglades into Florida Bay. But that has kind of been choked off over the years for different reasons. We're now restoring that flow down to Florida Bay. And so the water in Florida Bay is much better than when I became governor. We've had fewer algae blooms than I think probably in any four-year period in modern Florida. But a lot of it is just making sure you have the infrastructure in place to clean water and to be able to put it where it needs to go and not have dirty water going where we don't want it to go.

transcript: So here's what I can tell you. We just ranked number one by Heritage Foundation for Education Freedom. We've always been ranked number one for Education Choice.
